input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "requires",
 "proof_obligation": "initiation",
 "diagnosis": "Function countMin lacks a precondition bounding i. Its ensures clause uses the slice v[0..i] and its body indexes v[i-1], both of which are ill-formed when i < 0 or i > v.Length (e.g. i = -1). Adding 'requires 0 <= i <= v.Length' makes the slice and index well-defined; recursive calls with i-1 (when i > 0) and the call sites in mCountMin (1 <= i <= v.Length) satisfy it."}
EOF
sed -i '14a\ requires 0<=i<=v.Length' program.dfy && sed -n 12,17p program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

content.text:
`program.dfy` now verifies: Dafny reports "4 verified, 0 errors".

**Problem:** The function `countMin` had no precondition limiting `i`. Its postcondition takes the slice `v[0..i]` (line 15) and its body reads `v[i-1]` (line 18). Neither is valid when `i` is outside `0..v.Length`, which is what the counterexample shows with `i = -1`.

**Fix:** I added one line to `countMin`:
```dafny
requires 0<=i<=v.Length
```
This makes the slice and the index valid, and nothing else needed to change. The recursive calls use `i-1` only when `i > 0`, so they meet the new requirement. The calls in `mCountMin` meet it too, because its loop invariant keeps `0 < i <= v.Length`.

`diagnosis.json` records this as a missing `requires` on `countMin`. I filed it under "initiation" because the task's categories don't include one for "the spec isn't well-formed", and that was the closest fit.
